clue.text: Exterior of empty cafeteria in decline

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, so the second word wraps around the first

parts.note: to decline is to fade away

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: only the end letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: The outside of a run-down, deserted cafeteria looks shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters go inside FADE after its first letter: F-CA-ADE gives FACADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is the front face of a building, its outward exterior.

clue.text: Downy winged creature circling university very loudly

indicators.note: something circling goes all the way round, so the insect's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a fly is a winged insect
U is the standard abbreviation for university
fortissimo, marked ff in music, means very loudly

explanation.surface: A soft little insect buzzes loudly round a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: ff is the musical marking for fortissimo, an instruction to play very loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluffy and downy both describe something covered in soft fine feathers or hair.

clue.text: Sound from pet barking at a curlew

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, and crazy letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A household dog yaps at a wading bird, a curlew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' suggests the pet is a dog, but the answer is a cat's noise; barking is just the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterwaul is the wailing howl a cat makes, so it is a noise from a household animal.

clue.text: Agricultural deity encountered among hoofed animals

indicators.note: being among things means standing in their midst, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: deer are hoofed animals
encountered means met

explanation.surface: A farming goddess runs into a herd of hoofed beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeter is the Greek goddess of the harvest and grain, the deity of farming.

clue.text: Check old boy renovated castle

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: a renovated building has been reworked, so these letters get rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former pupil restored an old castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A check is something that halts progress, which is what an obstacle does.

clue.text: Hardly setting base down before server passing one drink

indicators.note: base is the mathematical constant e, and setting it further down the word shifts that letter one place later

parts.note: hardly means barely

indicators.note: passing something means going by without stopping, so that letter is skipped

parts.note: a waiter serves at table
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A waiter, barely managing to put down a tray, walks past someone with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the E of BARELY one place down gives BARLEY; WAITER without its I gives WATER. E is the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: Barley water is a soft drink made by boiling barley, often flavoured with lemon, popular in Britain.

clue.text: Case for racket turned up, sufficient for squash

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning letters up means reading them from bottom to top
the case of a word is its outside, so only its outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
ample means sufficient

explanation.surface: A racket cover pushed up proves good enough for a game of squash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash' looks like the racket sport, but it is the verb, to crush underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample something is to crush or flatten it, which is to squash it.

clue.text: Beam of light hit facial feature on king

parts.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A boxer lands a punch on a king's jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed below, so K follows CHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A chink of light is a narrow ray that slips through a small gap.

clue.text: Remark is penned by established writer

indicators.note: something penned is shut inside an enclosure, so these words sit within the other

parts.note: est. is the abbreviation for established
to remark is to say
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comment is written down by a well-known author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' suggests writing, fitting the author, but here it means enclosed as in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist is a writer who composes essays.

clue.text: Period of operating Muppet film set at regular points

indicators.note: taking letters at regular points means every other letter, at even intervals

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A Muppet movie is shot at set intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptime is the time a computer or machine spends running, as opposed to downtime.

clue.text: Worry in attempts to make pacts

indicators.note: one word goes in the other, being enclosed by it

parts.note: attempts are tries
to eat at someone is to worry or trouble them

explanation.surface: Anxious efforts to strike agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry' reads as a noun, but it is the verb: something that eats at you worries you.
explanation.definitionFit: Treaties are formal agreements between states, that is, pacts.

clue.text: Sample speciality wraps Greek character originally sourced

indicators.note: to wrap something is to surround it, so the first word encloses what follows

parts.note: a forte is someone's speciality
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A specialist dish contains a Greek ingredient from its source.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample of something to come.

clue.text: Protected Farage in conflict with dudes

indicators.note: things in conflict are in disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nigel Farage, the British populist politician, gets guarded while clashing with some lads.
explanation.definitionFit: Safeguarded means kept from harm, which is protected.

clue.text: Post Office locker without much room

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office
a key is something that locks

explanation.surface: A post office storage locker is cramped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locker' looks like a storage cupboard, but it is read as a thing that locks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pokey describes a room that is small and cramped, with little space.

clue.text: Needing to change size — after power tool for fiddly jobs

indicators.note: letters that need to change must be put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A power tool must be resized to manage delicate work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After power' reads as a P placed first, but both words are part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweezers are small pincers used for delicate, intricate tasks like removing splinters.

clue.text: Mouths busy crane fed in tangled nest

indicators.note: something fed in is put inside, so these letters go within the other group
busy suggests bustling activity, stirring these letters about

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: tangled things are jumbled, so these letters are mixed up too

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bustling crane bird feeds hungry beaks in a messy nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouths' suggests chicks' beaks, but it means openings such as cave mouths.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrances are ways in, as are the mouths of caves, rivers or tunnels.

clue.text: One nursing commercial objective upset world of scholars

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close, so the first word cradles the next

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an aim is an objective

explanation.surface: Someone tending a business goal ends up disrupting the scholarly world.
explanation.walkthrough: An ace is the one in a pack of cards, which is why 'One' can stand for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the community and environment of universities and scholarly research.

clue.text: Agreeing not to continue career with IT, resigns

parts.note: a calling is a vocation or career
taken as written
someone who resigns quits

explanation.surface: A worker in a tech career decides to resign and stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling it quits is an idiom for agreeing to stop doing something.

clue.text: Immediate and popular way to obtain bronzed look

parts.note: something popular is in

indicators.note: to obtain something is to take hold of it, so the word for way holds the next piece inside

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a tan is a bronzed look

explanation.surface: A quick, fashionable method of getting a suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes a fake instant tan; the tan goes inside the abbreviation for street, between its S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant means happening at once, without delay, that is, immediate.

clue.text: Many a Parisian welcoming politician with support

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the French word surrounds what follows

parts.note: un is French for a
an MP is a Member of Parliament
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Plenty of French people greet a politician with their backing.
explanation.walkthrough: A tee is the peg that supports a golf ball before it is struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for a great many, an indefinitely large number.

clue.text: Scoffed starters of jellied eels before daughter

indicators.note: starters are the opening parts, so each word gives only its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of each word
ere is an old word for before
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone wolfed down the first jellied eels, a Cockney dish of eels in jelly, before their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' suggests eating greedily, but it means mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to mock, and jeered means mocked with taunts.

clue.text: Spoke about five backing singers

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters are read from right to left
about means around, so the word for spoke goes around the numeral

parts.note: spoke means said
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A spokesperson talked about five backing singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing singers' looks like one phrase, but 'backing' is the reversal signal and 'singers' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Divas are celebrated female opera singers, prima donnas.

clue.text: Clean sides of the toilet all over

indicators.note: over means flipped, so everything reads from the other end
the sides of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
lav is short for lavatory, a toilet

explanation.surface: Clean the toilet everywhere, sides included.
explanation.definitionFit: To valet a car is to clean it thoroughly inside and out.

clue.text: Transport opening from rear on a track

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reading from the rear means starting at the end of the word

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin
a lane is a track or narrow road

explanation.surface: A vehicle with a door at the back runs along a track.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the backward word follows A, then LANE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeroplane is a means of transport by air.

clue.text: Turning pan containing fat fowl

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the first word wraps around the second
turning a word round makes it run the other way

parts.note: to pan a show is to slam it, criticising it harshly
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A cook turns a frying pan full of fat with ducks in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' looks like a cooking vessel; it is the verb to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallards are common wild ducks, a kind of fowl.

clue.text: Sportsperson runs after receiver

parts.note: a fence is a receiver of stolen goods
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An athlete sprints after catching a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' suggests a sports catcher, but it is criminal slang for someone who handles stolen goods. The R goes after.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer is an athlete who competes in the sport of fencing with swords.

clue.text: Leaning position gaining power for cyclist ultimately

indicators.note: gaining one thing for another means it is taken in as a swap

parts.note: an attitude is a position or stance
P is the physics abbreviation for power

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cyclist, in the end, leans into position to gain power.
explanation.walkthrough: The second T of ATTITUDE is swapped for P.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaning is a natural inclination or talent, which is an aptitude.

clue.text: Remaining disgruntled leaving in the morning

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters drop out of the word

parts.note: a disgruntled person is unamused
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone still grumpy is leaving early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Unused things are left over and still available, that is, remaining.
